# A Fast Start Became a Complete Hanshin Win

On August 16, at Mazda Stadium, Hanshin took control of the game almost immediately.

In the first inning, Teruaki Sato hit a two-run home run to center field. Hanshin led 2-0 before the game had truly settled.

Starting pitcher Ryoto Ihara then gave that lead a strong base. He worked five innings, allowing only two hits and one run.

Hiroshima’s run came in the fifth inning. Elehuris Montero hit a solo home run, making the score 2-1. But that was the only run Hiroshima scored all night.

Hanshin did not stop at its early lead. The team added more runs in the seventh and eighth innings. The advantage grew, and the game moved away from a close finish.

The final score was Hiroshima 1, Hanshin 8.

It was a win that began with one powerful swing, but finished through steady work on both sides of the game.

### The lead was built in stages

Hanshin’s late offense came from more than the opening home run. Seishiro Sakamoto drove in a run in the seventh and another in the eighth. Pinch-hitter Fushimi also added an RBI in the seventh. The victory was extended step by step, rather than decided by one early moment alone.

### What the score shows—and what it does not

The result shows that Hiroshima did not produce a sustained scoring rally. Its only run came from a solo home run, with no larger inning following it. But the available facts do not show whether that control came from the relief pitchers, the defense, or a specific change after Ihara left. The safe conclusion is about the score, not one exact method.

## In one line…

Hanshin turned an early advantage into an 8-1 win, with Sato starting the attack and the team adding enough later to make the result clear.
